## Simulation Setup

```{python}
import ornstein_uhlenbeck.ou as ou
import numpy as np

params = ou.OUParams(
    theta = 3.0,
    mu = 100.0,
    sigma = 10.0
)

x0 = 90.0
dt = 0.01
n_steps = 1000
n_paths_visual = 15
n_paths_validation = 10000

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

t = ou.time_grid(dt, n_steps)
paths_visual = ou.simulate_paths(x0, params, dt, n_steps, n_paths_visual, rng)
paths_validation = ou.simulate_paths(x0, params, dt, n_steps, n_paths_validation, rng)

def apply_theme(fig):
    fig.update_layout(
        template="plotly_dark",
        paper_bgcolor="#111A22",
        plot_bgcolor="#111A22",
        font=dict(size=16),
        width=799,
        height=500,
        legend=dict(
            orientation="h",
            yanchor="bottom",
            y=1.02,
            xanchor="right",
            x=1,
        ),
    )
    return fig
```

## Simulating a single path

```{python}
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x = t,
        y = paths_visual[:,0],
        name = "Simulated path",
        mode = "lines",
    )
)

fig.add_hline(
    y = params.mu,
    line_dash = "dash",
    annotation_text = "Long-run mean",
)

fig.update_layout(
    title = "Single Ornstein-Uhlenbeck sample path",
    xaxis_title = "Time",
    yaxis_title = "State"
)

apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()
```

## Simulating multiple paths


```{python}
fig = go.Figure()

for i in range(paths_visual.shape[1]):
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x = t,
            y = paths_visual[:, i],
            mode = "lines",
            line = dict(width = 0.8),
            opacity = 0.4,
            showlegend = False,
        )
    )

fig.add_hline(
    y = params.mu,
    line_dash = "dash",
    annotation_text = "Long-run mean",
)

fig.update_layout(
    title = "Multiple Ornstein-Uhlenbeck sample path",
    xaxis_title = "Time",
    yaxis_title = "State"
)

apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()
```

## Mean validation

To verify the expectation 

- simulate many paths 
- compute empirical mean at time $t$
- compare this with the theoretical mean

```{python}
empirical_mean = paths_validation.mean(axis=1)
theoretical = ou.theoretical_mean(t, x0, params)

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=t,
        y=empirical_mean,
        name="Monte Carlo",
        mode="lines",
    )
)

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=t,
        y=theoretical,
        name="Theory",
        mode="lines",
        line=dict(dash="dash"),
    )
)

fig.update_layout(
    title="Validation of the theoretical mean",
    xaxis_title="Time",
    yaxis_title="Mean",
)

apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()
```

## Variance validation

Likewise for the variance

- simulate many paths 
- compute empirical variance at time $t$
- compare this with the theoretical variance

```{python}
empirical_variance = paths_validation.var(axis=1)
theoretical = ou.theoretical_variance(t, params)

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=t,
        y=empirical_variance,
        name="Monte Carlo",
    )
)

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=t,
        y=theoretical,
        name="Theory",
        line=dict(dash="dash"),
    )
)

fig.update_layout(
    title="Validation of the theoretical variance",
    xaxis_title="Time",
    yaxis_title="Variance",
)

apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()
```

## Stationary distribution

```{python}
from scipy.stats import norm

terminal = paths_validation[-1]

x = np.linspace(
    terminal.min(),
    terminal.max(),
    500,
)

pdf = norm.pdf(
    x,
    loc=params.mu,
    scale=np.sqrt(ou.stationary_variance(params)),
)

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(
    go.Histogram(
        x=terminal,
        histnorm="probability density",
        name="Simulation",
    )
)

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=x,
        y=pdf,
        name="Theoretical density",
        mode="lines",
    )
)

fig.update_layout(
    title="Stationary distribution",
    xaxis_title="State",
    yaxis_title="Density",
    bargap=0.05,
)

apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()
```
